question: What is progressive rendering?
answerGeneral: Progressive rendering is a set of techniques that make a page appear useful to the user as quickly as possible, rather than waiting for the entire page to load before showing anything. Key techniques: **lazy loading** (defer images/iframes below the fold with `loading="lazy"`); **above-the-fold prioritisation** (critical CSS inline, `<link rel=preload>` for key assets); **streaming HTML** (server sends chunks as they're ready — HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer, HTTP/2 server push); **skeleton screens** (show layout placeholders before data arrives); **prioritising visible content** (route-based code splitting). React 18's Suspense + streaming SSR is a modern framework-level implementation.
answerGeneralTr: Progressive rendering, tüm sayfanın yüklenmesini beklemek yerine sayfanın kullanıcıya mümkün olduğunca çabuk yararlı görünmesini sağlayan bir teknikler setidir. Temel teknikler: **lazy loading** (`loading="lazy"` ile ekran dışı resimleri/iframe'leri ertele); **fold üstü önceliklendirme** (kritik CSS inline, anahtar varlıklar için `<link rel=preload>`); **HTML akışı** (sunucu hazır oldukça parçalar gönderir); **iskelet ekranlar** (veriler gelmeden önce düzen yer tutucularını göster). React 18'in Suspense + streaming SSR, modern bir framework düzeyinde uygulamadır.

question: What are Web Components?
answerGeneral: Web Components is a suite of native browser APIs for creating reusable, encapsulated custom elements that work across any framework. The three pillars: (1) **Custom Elements** — define your own HTML tags with a JavaScript class (`class MyButton extends HTMLElement`); (2) **Shadow DOM** — an encapsulated DOM subtree with scoped CSS that doesn't bleed in or out; (3) **HTML Templates** (`<template>`, `<slot>`) — inert markup that is cloned when the component is used. Web Components are framework-agnostic — a component built once works in React, Angular, Vue, or plain HTML without modification.
answerGeneralTr: Web Components, herhangi bir framework'te çalışan yeniden kullanılabilir, kapsüllenmiş özel öğeler oluşturmak için yerel tarayıcı API'lerinin bir paketidir. Üç temel: (1) **Custom Elements** — bir JavaScript sınıfıyla kendi HTML etiketlerinizi tanımlayın; (2) **Shadow DOM** — içeri veya dışarı sızmayan kapsamlı CSS ile kapsüllenmiş bir DOM alt ağacı; (3) **HTML Templates** (`<template>`, `<slot>`) — bileşen kullanıldığında klonlanan inert işaretleme. Web Components framework-agnostiktir — bir kez oluşturulan bir bileşen React, Angular, Vue veya düz HTML'de değişiklik olmadan çalışır.

question: What is an IndexedDB?
answerGeneral: IndexedDB is a low-level, asynchronous, NoSQL key-value store built into browsers that can hold large amounts of structured data — including files, blobs, and complex JavaScript objects. Unlike localStorage (~5 MB, synchronous, string-only), IndexedDB has no practical size limit (browser-dependent, typically gigabytes), supports indexes for fast querying, transactions for data integrity, and works in Web Workers and Service Workers. Its raw API is callback/event-based and verbose — libraries like **Dexie.js** or **idb** wrap it in Promises. Used for offline-capable apps, caching API responses, and storing large datasets.
answerGeneralTr: IndexedDB, büyük miktarda yapılandırılmış veri — dosyalar, blob'lar ve karmaşık JavaScript nesneleri dahil — tutabilen düşük düzeyli, asenkron, NoSQL anahtar-değer bir tarayıcı deposudur. localStorage'ın (~5 MB, senkron, yalnızca string) aksine, IndexedDB'nin pratik bir boyut sınırı yoktur (tarayıcıya bağlı, genellikle gigabaytlar), hızlı sorgulama için indeksleri, veri bütünlüğü için işlemleri destekler ve Web Workers ile Service Workers'da çalışır. Ham API'si karmaşıktır — **Dexie.js** veya **idb** gibi kütüphaneler bunu Promise'larla sarar.

question: What is accessibility & ARIA role means in a web application?
answerGeneral: Accessibility (a11y) means building web applications usable by people with disabilities — visual, motor, cognitive, or auditory. WCAG 2.1 defines the standard across four principles: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust. ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications) is a W3C spec of attributes (`role`, `aria-*`) that supplement HTML semantics for dynamic content and custom widgets that lack native equivalents. First rule of ARIA: don't use it if native HTML already provides the semantics (`<button>` over `<div role=button>`). Key ARIA concepts: roles (what the element is), states (`aria-expanded`, `aria-checked`), and properties (`aria-label`, `aria-describedby`).
answerPersonal: At Butlin's, I integrated ReciteMe — an accessibility toolbar that handles font resizing, colour overlays, text-to-speech, and translation. This required auditing our component library for WCAG 2.1 AA compliance, particularly around colour contrast ratios, focus management, and keyboard navigation. Working within ReciteMe's API constraints pushed me to ensure our semantic HTML was solid first, so their tools could operate on a clean foundation.

question: Could you generate a public key in HTML?
answerGeneral: The `<keygen>` element (HTML5) was designed to generate a public/private key pair in the browser and submit the public key via a form — the private key was stored in the browser's key store. It was deprecated in HTML5.1 and removed from all browsers by 2019 because it was poorly adopted and had security concerns. The modern equivalent is the **Web Crypto API** (`window.crypto.subtle`), which provides proper asymmetric key generation (`generateKey`, `exportKey`, `sign`, `verify`) without a dedicated HTML element — all in JavaScript with far more flexibility and control.
answerGeneralTr: `<keygen>` öğesi (HTML5), tarayıcıda bir genel/özel anahtar çifti oluşturmak ve genel anahtarı bir form aracılığıyla göndermek için tasarlandı. HTML5.1'de kullanımdan kaldırıldı ve 2019 yılına kadar tüm tarayıcılardan kaldırıldı. Modern eşdeğeri, asimetrik anahtar oluşturmayı (`generateKey`, `exportKey`, `sign`, `verify`) çok daha fazla esneklik ve kontrolle sağlayan **Web Crypto API**'si (`window.crypto.subtle`)'dir.

question: Why do I need a doctype and what does it do?
answerGeneral: The DOCTYPE declaration (`<!DOCTYPE html>`) is a mandatory preamble that tells the browser to render the document in full standards mode. Without it, browsers enter quirks mode — a backward-compatibility emulation of pre-standards rendering (IE5/Netscape behaviour) where the box model, font inheritance, and many CSS features behave differently. The HTML5 doctype is intentionally minimal to avoid requiring a URL to a DTD (unlike older HTML 4.01 or XHTML doctypes). It is a processing instruction for the HTML parser, not a tag. Its presence before any whitespace or content is critical — some older browsers fall into quirks mode even if the doctype appears on line 2.
detailMd:
## Why the parser needs it

In the late 1990s, browsers implemented their own non-standard CSS/layout behaviour. When standards arrived, browsers needed a way to distinguish old pages (that relied on the old behaviour) from new pages (that expected standards). The doctype toggle was invented for this:

```
No doctype / unknown doctype → quirks mode
<!DOCTYPE html>              → full standards mode
Some old XHTML doctypes      → almost standards mode
```

## Box model difference — the key consequence

```css
/* Full standards mode (CSS box model) */
.box { width: 200px; padding: 20px; border: 5px solid; }
/* Total rendered width: 200 + 20*2 + 5*2 = 250px */

/* Quirks mode (IE5 box model) */
/* Total rendered width: 200px (padding + border are counted inside width) */
/* This is equivalent to: box-sizing: border-box */
```

## Detecting the current mode

```js
console.log(document.compatMode);
// 'CSS1Compat'  → full standards (or almost standards)
// 'BackCompat'  → quirks mode
```

## Why it must be first

```html
<!-- ❌ Whitespace before doctype can trigger quirks in some browsers -->
  <!DOCTYPE html>

<!-- ✅ Doctype as the absolute first content -->
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
```

IE6 and some older Gecko versions fell into quirks mode if anything — even a BOM or XML prolog — preceded the doctype.

## HTML5 vs older doctypes

```html
<!-- HTML5 — simple, no DTD -->
<!DOCTYPE html>

<!-- HTML 4.01 Strict — references a DTD URL -->
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01//EN"
  "http://www.w3.org/TR/html4/strict.dtd">

<!-- The DTD URL was never actually fetched by browsers -->
<!-- HTML5 simplified this by removing the DTD requirement entirely -->
```
answerGeneralTr: DOCTYPE bildirimi (`<!DOCTYPE html>`), tarayıcıya belgeyi tam standartlar modunda render etmesini söyleyen zorunlu bir önsözdür. Bu olmadan, tarayıcılar quirks moduna girer — standart öncesi render'ın geriye dönük uyumluluk emülasyonu. HTML5 doctype'ı, eski HTML 4.01 veya XHTML doctypelarının aksine bir DTD URL'si gerektirmemek için kasıtlı olarak minimaldir. HTML ayrıştırıcısı için bir işlem talimatıdır, etiket değildir.
